findings.body:
`DELETE /users/<user>` no longer has any authorization check. There is no `before_request` hook, token check, or other gate in this app, so any caller can remove any name from `USERS` and receive 204. Cleanup jobs hitting 403 should authenticate as an allowed identity (admin or a dedicated job role) and that identity should be checked here; do not leave the destructive route open.

Note that `require_role` compared `ROLES.get(user)` to the path parameter, so it was checking the *target* user rather than the caller — restoring a caller-based check is the real fix.

summary:
Removing `@require_role("admin")` from `DELETE /users/<user>` leaves user deletion with no authorization at all. Anyone who can reach the route can delete any user, which is a production-blocking security and data-loss regression. The 403s on cleanup jobs should be fixed by authenticating the job as a privileged identity (or a dedicated cleanup role) and checking that identity, while keeping an authorization gate on this handler.

`require_role` itself inspects `ROLES.get(user)` where `user` is the path parameter, so it was gating on the *target* account rather than the caller. That likely explains viewer-account 403s, but dropping the decorator is still the wrong fix.

**Recommendation:** request-changes
